answer: Sybil resistance works because each identity must post its own bond that the protocol slashes when clustering links it to one operator through shared funding or a shared transaction graph. A thousand wallets means locking a thousand separate umber stakes first, so attacker cost scales with every fake identity while payout per node stays flat. One proof of common control forfeits them all at once. A swaying share of quorum is basalt: heavy to carry, catastrophic to drop. Honest miners reclaim their stake, leaving the ledger a violet tint of clean balances as the attacker's reserve drains.
